description: The REVERSE-SEARCH relational operators of the START KEY phrase - LESS, NOT GREATER, LESS OR EQUAL and their symbols (<, NOT >, <=) - ISO 14.9.41.4 GR9 b) (relative: 'searching the file in reverse order') and GR17 d) (indexed: 'the file is searched in reverse order'). COBOL-85's START searches FORWARD only - the set GR9 a) / GR17 c) still name first, which NOT LESS and NOT < fold into, so they stay legal at 85 (conformance:cases/14.9.41-START/pb370_start_forward_operators); A.3 item 39 binds the reverse set to READ ... PREVIOUS in ONE sentence as ONE reverse-access processor capability, and READ PREVIOUS is read-previous-2002. THE EDGE IS DERIVED, NOT QUOTED (the repo holds no 1985 or 2002 text, ratified decision #1): IBM Enterprise COBOL, a COBOL-85 implementation, admits only the forward set, and the 459 NIST CCVS-85 programs write only EQUAL, GREATER and NOT LESS. Gated on RECOGNITION in the VersionConformancePass parse arm (VisitStartKeyPhrase, the operator folded by ConditionBinder.MapOperator, the same fold KeyedIoBinder binds), so an ill-organized or unbindable START still names the edition (kb/Work PB370).
display: a reverse-search START KEY operator (LESS, NOT GREATER, LESS OR EQUAL)
citation: ISO §2023:14.9.41.4 GR9 b) / GR17 d) (the reverse-search operator set); §2023:A.3 item 39 (READ PREVIOUS and the reverse START operators, one processor-dependent capability); a COBOL-2002 introduction (derived)
vcr: provisional 2002 edge (decision-1 policy), bound to read-previous-2002 by A.3 item 39
source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. VMSTRV.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
FILE-CONTROL.
    SELECT F ASSIGN TO "vmstrv" ORGANIZATION IS RELATIVE
        ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC RELATIVE KEY IS W-K.
DATA DIVISION.
FILE SECTION.
FD F.
01 R PIC X(10).
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 W-K PIC 9(4).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    OPEN INPUT F.
    START F KEY IS LESS THAN W-K INVALID KEY DISPLAY "E".
    CLOSE F.
    STOP RUN.
